content_en.prompt: Beavers practice climbing steep hills in a single-file line, each carrying a ladder. At a steep climb, the beaver at the front holds up their ladder for others; all ladder-holding beavers stay in place until every other beaver has climbed to the top, then each ladder-holder climbs up using their own ladder, joining the line last, in the order they held their ladder (last ladder-holder set up joins first among the holders). Six beavers hike a terrain with three hills of different heights (levels).
content_en.question: Which beaver will be the first one to reach the flag (i.e. what is the final beaver order after all three hills)?
content_en.explanation: Starting in order 123456: at the first hill (3 levels), beavers 1, 2, 3 hold ladders at levels 1-3 while 4, 5, 6 climb to the top in that order; then 3, 2, 1 climb up in that order, giving order 456321. At the second hill (4 levels), beavers 4, 5, 6, 3 hold ladders while 2, 1 climb to the top; then 3, 6, 5, 4 climb up, giving order 213654. At the third hill (2 levels), beavers 2, 1 hold ladders while 3, 6, 5, 4 climb to the top; then 1, 2 climb up, giving the final order 365412 — so beaver 3 arrives first.
content_en.ct_explanation: How the beavers climb reflects both a stack and a queue in computer science. A stack works like physically stacking objects: you add to the top, and only the top item is accessible, so the first item placed is the last one removed — described as first-in-last-out (FILO); this is how beavers set up their ladders. A queue works like people lining up for tickets: the first person in line is served first, so the first item placed in is the first one out — first-in-first-out (FIFO); this describes the order in which beavers climb up each hill. Students apply pattern recognition to work out the order in which beavers set up ladders and climb, and algorithmic thinking to follow the rules and trace the beavers' order through the whole hike.

content_zh.prompt: 海狸們排成一列練習爬陡坡，每隻都扛著一把梯子。遇到陡坡時，排在最前面的海狸會舉起梯子讓其他海狸爬上去；所有正在舉梯子的海狸都會留在原地，直到其他所有海狸都爬到坡頂為止，接著每隻舉梯子的海狸再用自己的梯子爬上去，依照「舉梯子的順序」加入隊伍最後方（最晚舉起梯子的海狸，會最先爬上去、排在舉梯海狸裡最前面）。六隻海狸要走一段地形，中途要爬三座高度（層數）不同的山丘。
content_zh.question: 哪一隻海狸會最先抵達旗子（也就是爬完三座山丘之後，海狸的最終順序是什麼）？
content_zh.explanation: 一開始的順序是123456：在第一座山丘（3層），海狸1、2、3分別在第1、2、3層舉梯子，海狸4、5、6依序爬到坡頂；接著3、2、1依序爬上去，得到順序456321。在第二座山丘（4層），海狸4、5、6、3舉梯子，2、1先爬到坡頂；接著3、6、5、4依序爬上去，得到順序213654。在第三座山丘（2層），海狸2、1舉梯子，3、6、5、4先爬到坡頂；接著1、2爬上去，得到最終順序365412——所以最先抵達的是3號海狸。
content_zh.ct_skills: 樣式辨識、演算法思維（Pattern recognition, Algorithmic Thinking）
content_zh.cs_domain: 資料、資料結構與表示法
content_zh.ct_explanation: 海狸爬山丘的方式，同時反映了電腦科學裡「堆疊」和「佇列」這兩種資料結構。堆疊的運作方式，就像現實中把物品一個個疊起來：你把東西加到最上面，也只能拿最上面那個，所以最先放上去的東西，會是最後才被拿走的——這叫做「先進後出」（FILO）；海狸架設梯子的方式正是如此。佇列的運作方式，則像排隊買票：排在最前面的人最先被服務，所以最先進入佇列的項目，也會最先被取出——這叫做「先進先出」（FIFO）；海狸爬上每座山丘的順序，正好符合這個模式。學生要運用樣式辨識，才能推算出海狸架梯子和爬坡的順序；也要運用演算法思維，才能依照規則、追蹤海狸在整趟健行過程中的順序變化。
